title: Notion's Token Town — Sarah Sachs, Notion
talk_summary: Sarah Sachs of Notion argues that AI cost is a structural barrier and that companies should stay model-agnostic, route traffic by cost-per-capability-per-second, use open-weight models for moderate tasks, and replace LLM calls with deterministic code where possible. She also stresses sandboxing, governance, and multi-agent orchestration as the real near-term challenges.

takeaways.what_they_do: Notion's auto-model routes ~75% of traffic to cheaper models and reserves frontier models for genuinely hard tasks, explicitly avoiding sending all traffic to the latest Opus.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It is a huge miss to send all of these to the latest opus model... When you triage an email inbox, if we're charging you to do that on Opus, we're ripping you off
takeaways.numbers: ~75% of traffic handled by auto model

takeaways.technique: CPUs over GPUs / deterministic code instead of LLM calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Replace LLM calls with plain code for deterministic jobs like CSV-to-PDF, CLI tool calls, and SQL queries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You don't need an LLM to turn a CSV into a PDF. You don't need an LLM to talk to notion tool calls if we have a CLI. You definitely don't need an LLM to do deterministic SQL queries.

takeaways.what_they_do: Build the harness for model interoperability so any model can be swapped per thread or per task without lock-in, and keep open-weight models as a credible fallback.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Stay model agnostic. Have different models and capabilities in your system so that at any point if pricing seems unfair or untenable, you are not out of business.

takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate cost-per-capability-per-second over whole agent trajectories (e.g., web search) rather than per-call latency or price, to pick providers correctly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The granularity of this eval is what lets us make the best decisions for our customers because we understand all of the trade-offs on entire trajectories, not just single calls.

takeaways.technique: Sandboxes for determinism and token economics
takeaways.what_they_do: Run agent work in sandboxes/computers to get determinism and reduce token spend versus free-form agent execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Same with sandboxes and computers... it really is something that builds better determinism in your product and also better token economics for your customers

takeaways.technique: Cross-model review and collaborative task docs
takeaways.what_they_do: After one agent opens a PR, a different model (Codex) reviews it; tasks live in an active collaborative doc where agents and humans scope, ask questions, and hand off.
